stemBlocks: Sodium feredetate trihydrate and iron(II) sulfate can both be used to treat iron deficiency. The formula for sodium feredetate trihydrate is:
Sodium feredetate trihydrate is used as a solution. $5.00 \text{ cm}^3$ of this solution contains $210.5 \text{ mg}$ of sodium feredetate trihydrate.
Iron(II) sulfate is used in tablet form. One iron tablet contains $63.0 \text{ mg}$ of iron(II) ions.
What volume of sodium feredetate trihydrate solution would give the same mass of iron as one iron(II) sulfate tablet?
